function: Over-the-air aggregation of federated updates through a MIMO multiple access channel, plus neural lossy distributed source coding of edge updates over the fronthaul (pp. 4, 9-10).
system: MIMO Cloud-RAN: 3 APs with 8 antennas, 20 devices with 3 antennas, block fading, MIMO multiple access uplink; no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 11-12, Table I).
method: Federated learning of a small CNN classifier; beamformers by alternating optimization and majorization-minimization; K-layer neural decoder for L-DSC trained by backpropagation on Gaussian samples (pp. 8-10).
data_channel: Custom simulator: path loss with i.i.d. complex Gaussian small-scale fading, 3-D device layout; FL data are MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10; no 3GPP or measured channel (pp. 10-11).
test_conditions: Same simulated channel for training and testing; separate runs for NT=2-16 antennas, power, fronthaul rate, data heterogeneity Q; test accuracy on the same dataset's test set (pp. 11-13).
baselines: Unoptimized L-DSC with dataset-size weights, simple quantization, stochastic quantization [16], DNN-based L-DSC [34], practical L-DSC without side information; error-free bound and optimized L-DSC as references (pp. 11-13).
metrics: Test accuracy versus training round on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10; simulation time per communication round (Table II) (pp. 12-13).
complexity: Orders of complexity per device, AP and optimization (pp. 7, 9); L-DSC encoder O(N^2 sigma), decoder O(NA N K M) (p. 10); runtime per round, Table II (p. 13).
q1_support: p. 11: "modeled as i.i.d. circularly symmetric complex Gaussian random variables with zero-mean and unit-variance" with a path-loss term; a custom simulator, and the paper never mentions 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured channels.
q2_support: p. 12: "we change the number of antennas at the transmitter side while keeping the number of receiver antennas fixed at NR = 8"; each setting is a separate training run (test accuracy versus training round), and no model trained in one condition is tested in another.
q3_support: p. 13: "both the encoding and decoding functions are based on deep neural networks as described in [34]"; p. 13: "each AP quantizes its edge update using the method in [16]"; p. 13: "the proposed practical L-DSC outperforms other baseline scheme across all heterogeneous settings".
q4_support: p. 10: "The encoder complexity of practical L-DSC, dominated by the compression in (36)" is O(N^2 sigma) and the decoder is O(NA N K M); p. 9: "the overall complexity of solving our proposed optimization problem" is given as an order; p. 13: Table II lists the simulation time per communication round.
q5_support: p. 10: "We test federated image classification on three datasets" (MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10), which are learning-task datasets; the channel is simulated and the paper gives no link to code or data.
notes: Included in area 7. The edge aggregation is over the air (p. 3: signals of the devices of one AP are sent over shared resources, "a.k.a., over-the-air computation") and the transmit and receive beamformers are optimized in problem (27) (p. 8); the global aggregation over the wired fronthaul is digital (L-DSC) but belongs to the same OA-FL framework. The learned elements are the FL-trained CNN and the neural L-DSC decoder; beamforming itself is classical optimization. Table I and Table II were not in the extracted text, so they were read from the page images of pp. 11 and 13 (NT=3, NR=8, alpha=3.8, power 5 W, Delta=30 m, noise -70 dBm; times per round). Points for the reviewer: (1) q3 rests on the DNN-based L-DSC of [34], a task-oriented communication design that the authors apply to this aggregation problem (p. 13), and on stochastic quantization [16] as the earlier non-learned design; simple quantization and the unoptimized and no-side-information variants are the authors' own and are not counted. (2) The text cites [33] for the channel model (p. 11) but [33] in the list is Fashion-MNIST, so the origin of the model is unclear; it is custom either way, so q1 is 0.
